subject: Operator certification & runbook request for private deployment
messages:
From: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@mednova.com>
To: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@mednova.com, sanjay@mednova.com
Date: Sun, 28 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Operator certification & runbook request for private deployment

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're preparing internal procurement and security packets for a Private deployment (VPC + customer-managed operator) and need a few artifacts from Redwood to move forward with our legal/ops approval: 

- A sample "operator runbook" (technical playbook) showing handover, snapshoting/witnessing steps, and rollback procedures.
- Evidence of operator certification or qualification (could be test-accounts, runbook signoff, or a short operator attestation).
- Clarification on license boundary language: will the Order Form / MSA permit a verified operator to run scripted maintenance tasks and limited console access, or do we need a separate operator access addendum?
- A short list of proposed audit windows and what evidence you can provide (snapshots, logs, chain-of-custody) for compliance review.

Attached is our Security Questionnaire (partial) — fields we couldn't answer until we confirm operator scope. Can you share a sample runbook + any existing attestation template by EOD Thursday our time? If there's an internal legal contact for redlines we should loop in, please include them.

Best,
Daniel
Daniel Cho
Head of Procurement
Mednova Systems
Attachments: Mednova_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

From: mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai <mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@mednova.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operator certification & runbook request for private deployment

Hi Daniel — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Lauren (legal), Rishi (security/ops), and Alex (onprem infra) so they can weigh in on the redline and evidence items.

Quick answers and timeline from our side: 
- We can provide a redacted sample operator runbook (runbook-template.docx) that includes: operator roles, daily maintenance checklist, snapshoting/witness steps, emergency rollback steps, and test access procedures. Expect that in ~24–36 hours.
- Operator attestation: we have a short Operator Capability Statement (one-page) that an operator signs after a shadowed run. We can adapt language for your procurement team.
- License boundary: our standard MSA + Order Form includes a "limited operator activities" clause; however, for private deployments customers often ask for a narrow Operator Access Addendum that defines allowed CLI/console actions and a temporary audit window. Legal will propose specific language.
- Evidence for audits: we can provide time-stamped snapshots, AWS/GCP audit logs (where applicable), runbook change history, and a signed witnessing statement for snapshot ingestion. For chain-of-custody we typically use a sealed snapshot workflow plus attestations.

Can you confirm the expected retention window for evidence (30/90/365 days) and whether Mednova requires an on-site witness or a remote video-based witness? That affects the runbook samples we send.

Regards,
Mateo Alvarez
Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 08:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operator certification & runbook request for private deployment

Mateo — thanks, that's helpful. A few clarifications from procurement/security: 

- Evidence retention: we need 90 days of accessible artifacts for initial procurement review (may extend to 1 year for final contract).
- Witnessing: remote video-based witnessing is acceptable for our security team, but we also want the option to request an on-site technical witness for initial snapshot handoff for at least one onboarding event.
- Operator activities: acceptable scope would be (a) scripted maintenance and patch application, (b) snapshot creation and transfer under witness, (c) emergency hotfix pushes via pre-approved runbook steps. No interactive data exploration or model retraining.

Attached a short spreadsheet that shows the minimal operator actions we'd like enumerated. We can accept a concise attestation template (one page) and a signed runbook checklist in lieu of multi-page certificates.

Can legal propose a short Order Form addendum and a one-sentence MSA carrier clause that locks the operator scope? If so, we can route for signature and move to DocuSign.

Thanks —
Daniel
Attachments: operator-access-expectations.xlsx

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Cho <daniel.cho@mednova.com>, mateo.alvarez@redwood.ai
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, alex_martinez@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 Nov 2027 15:06:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Operator certification & runbook request for private deployment

Hi Daniel — looping in legal & ops alignment. Appreciate the clear constraints; we've drafted a short package that should address procurement and audit concerns. Summary of proposed deliverables and MSA/Order Form language below. Full redline is attached (redline_summary_MSAA-OF.docx) and I posted the redline to DocuSign at the link above for easier review.

Proposed deliverables (to attach as exhibits to the Order Form):
- Exhibit A: Operator Runbook (redacted) — includes snapshot witness procedure, emergency rollback checklist, maintenance windows, and operator ACLs.
- Exhibit B: Operator Attestation Template — one-page attestation signed by the operator after completion of shadowed onboarding.
- Exhibit C: Evidence Retention & Audit Playbook — defines 90-day retention for all audit artifacts, 1-year cold retention for snapshots, and chain-of-custody steps.

MSA/Order Form redline highlights (high level):
- License/Operational Boundary: add a short clause permitting operator-performed "Limited Maintenance Activities" as defined in Exhibit A; explicitly prohibit interactive data access and model training unless mutually agreed.
- Audit/Witnessing: customer may request remote witnessing; on-site witnessing permitted once during initial onboarding with reasonable notice and travel cost allocation.
- Snapshot Custody: define sealed snapshot transfer and signed witness statement upon ingestion; Redwood to retain cryptographic evidence for 1 year.
- Escrow-like requirement: we cannot provide full escrow of runtime binaries, but propose a narrow "witnessed snapshot" and operator attestation workflow as a compromise. If Mednova needs software escrow, we'll need to scope separately (timelines/costs).
- Order Form: add a 1-paragraph addendum that enumerates Exhibits A–C and attaches the Operator Attestation requirement as an Order Form obligation.

Next steps: 
1) Please confirm acceptance of the high-level approach (Exhibits A–C and the one-paragraph OF addendum).
2) If accepted, Mateo/ops will send the redacted runbook and attestation template by EOD tomorrow.
3) Legal will follow with a tracked-redline MSA + Order Form; we recommend limited back-and-forth and to mark a single commercial redline window to accelerate signature.
